name: Aggravation Speed
description: Aggravation is a two-player speed-matching game where players rapidly cover same-rank matches in expanding face-up rows.
deck: Standard 52-card deck split into two 26-card decks

overview.description: Aggravation is a two-player speed-matching game where players rapidly cover same-rank matches in expanding face-up rows.
overview.deck: Standard 52-card deck split into two 26-card decks

history.origins: Aggravation is documented as a California Speed family variant with expanding rows rather than fixed 2x4 layout.
timeline: Late 20th century: Speed-family games spread through schools and casual play.
Modern: Aggravation and Frustration variants remain popular reflex games.
history.cultural: Known for high tempo and the win call 'Aggravation!' when deck runs out and final match is found.
history.evolution: Compared with California Speed, players extend rows until matches appear, then cascade-cover matches rapidly.

setup.deck: One 52-card deck split equally into 26-card face-down player piles.
setup.dealing: Players simultaneously deal one face-up card each to begin rows, extending rows until matches occur.
setup.equipment: Deck and flat table space for two parallel rows.

rules.objective: Be first to empty your deck and legally call 'Aggravation!' on a live match.
rules.gameplay: Players simultaneously extend rows from their decks. Any time equal ranks appear anywhere in layout, a player may cover matching cards with new cards from own deck. Cascades continue while matches exist. When no matches remain, both extend rows again. A player with empty deck wins by tapping a valid match and calling 'Aggravation!'.
keyRules: Matches are by rank only; suits are irrelevant.
If no matches exist, rows are extended equally until a match appears.
A player with one last card must use it on a match, then find another match to call win.
If one player is out and no match exists, opponent continues dealing until a match appears.

strategy.basic: Scan both rows continuously instead of tunnel-visioning your own cards.
strategy.intermediate: Minimize hand-travel distance between likely matching zones to improve reaction speed.
strategy.advanced: Exploit cascade timing by planning immediate follow-up covers after first match contact.
tips: Use both hands for far-separated match pairs.
Keep rhythm between scanning and dealing so dead periods are short.

variations.name: Frustration
variations.description: When one player runs out, both scoop local rows and restart race with remaining cards until threshold is reached.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Frustration is documented only in prose; engine parameter differences are not yet modeled as structured overrides.

variations.name: California Speed
variations.description: Fixed 2x4 layout variant instead of growing rows.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: California Speed variant is described narratively; distinct engine overrides have not been wired yet.

scoring.description: Single-hand winner game determined by first valid aggravation call.
scoring.winCondition: First player to empty deck and call Aggravation on a valid match wins.

synthesis.shortDescription: A simultaneous reaction game of spotting and covering rank matches.
